name: Foundry Floor

acceptance.statement: The pack’s asset map marks all 31 models accepted: each was accepted by the scene coordinator’s review of its author’s delivery, and the scene’s intake checked its bytes and SHA-256. The owner has not reviewed this pack; it stays in production until then.
acceptance.source: data/assets.json (status accepted for every entity) and the Foundry Floor FF2 report, intake section

licenseScope: CC0-1.0 covers authored asset content only, to the extent of the owner’s rights. Kiln and any software that opens these files retain their own licenses.
licenceNote: The licence text was written by the Foundry Floor scene’s staging, because the author folders ship none. It names every model, its saved revision, its author folder and the SHA-256 of its GLB, and is published here unchanged.

conventions.frame: Metres. +X is forward, +Y up and +Z right.
conventions.lod: 24 of the 31 models keep a simpler far form in the same file, as a node named lod1. The file has no visibility flags, so a plain glTF viewer draws the detailed parts and lod1 together; lod1 lies inside the detailed parts’ bounding box. The Foundry Floor scene shows the detailed parts near and lod1 far.
conventions.hidden: Two models carry parts the scene hides when it loads them: the FOUP (waferStack) and the level section module (raisedFloor, ffuPlenum, cutFaceCaps_raisedFloor, cutFaceCaps_ffuWhite, cutFaceCaps_ffuHousing). They are part of the file, and a plain viewer draws them.
conventions.materials: No model uses a texture; colours are material factors. The pack’s accent colours are invented for readability and are not any maker’s livery.
conventions.clips: Animation clips carry no loop flags; the scene decides what loops.
conventions.source: The conventions are the pack’s own (data/assets.json); every figure on this page was read from the GLBs.

contents: The pack’s licence text, naming every model, its revision and its SHA-256
A delivery.json inventory with member hashes
downloads.compatibility: Standard glTF 2.0 with no extensions. A file with a far form keeps it beside its detailed parts as a node named lod1, and every part is visible, so a plain viewer draws both; the far form lies inside the detailed parts’ bounding box. Other engines are not qualified by this download.
